newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude - Lighter grades remain amply supplied.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude - Lighter grades remain amply supplied.

text.p: Limited buying kept light Asian crude market under pressure, while the heavier grades have found homes fairly easily, traders said on Thursday.

There were rumours of July Tapis being offered at levels as low as APPI even, or at a fixed price equating to a discount under APPI, but Malaysia said it was not showing any offer price for last July cargo, waiting for buyers' bid ideas.
An end July Dulang was confirmed traded between Malaysia and a US major, price level heard around OSP even.
But another Dulang trade, for early July, was probably done at OSP -15 from a shosha to a major in Thailand, traders said.
A Minas parcel was heard sold to China by an equity holder at ICP +25, although it was unclear when the trade actually took place.
But it did reflect the current market level, traders said.
In the Middle East market, the first August Qatar Marine cargoes started trading on Tuesday.
A US major bought a cargo from a shosha at a level of QGPC -40 or Dubai +10, whichever level is ultimately lower.
The same buyer also bought partial Qatar Marine cargo from a Europan major at QGPC -40/41, while another U.S. major heard bought a cargo from a trader at QGPC -45/48.
A U.S. major heard sold 1.5 million barrels of August Alaskan North Slope crude to its affiliated refineries in Japan, the first time that the company had sold ANS to the East.
Traders were uncertain if it was an arms length trade, with the price level heard to be Dubai even, c+f Japan.
West African crude trade had subsided, as the Brent/Dubai spread widens.
Only one Korean refiner was heard showing interest in West African cargoes and may have already covered by Wednesday evening, but details were not available.
